## Source
.design/m5/48-tpm-signing.md — Q1 + Q2 + decomposition PR 1.

## Surface (throwaway)
- Branch `spike/m48-tpm-esapi`. Runs `swtpm` + minimal seal+sign test via tss-esapi.
- Evidence written to `.design/m5/48-tpm-spike-results.md` at end.

## Measure
1. `tss-esapi` current crates.io version + maintainer responsiveness (commits last 6 months).
2. Linux 6.x kernel TPM driver compatibility.
3. K-256 (secp256k1) support — verify on at least 2 mainstream TPMs.
4. P-256 fallback support — verify universally.
5. Bluesky verifier: does it accept did:key declarations with P-256? Read the proto-blue or Bluesky verifier source.

## Rust-quality notes
- Throwaway — full bar relaxed. The LANDING code (#156+) follows full rust-quality.
- Per architect skill: time-box hard. 1-2 days max.

## External references
- tss-esapi current: https://crates.io/crates/tss-esapi
- swtpm setup: https://github.com/stefanberger/swtpm
- did:key spec (multicodec curve identifiers): https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-key/

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.design/m5/48-tpm-spike-results.md` exists with measurement data + recommendation.
